correctness.rationale: On adjacent-pair approval path the voter-sum welfare is 2k−x1−xm, and endpoint dominance swaps show PO iff x1≤x2 and xm≤xm−1. For quota q=(m−1)/k, every nonrepresented voter approving unelected candidate can form JR obstruction only when three consecutive candidates are all unelected and 1<q≤2; when q>2 groups too small, when q≤1 at most one vacancy so all voters represented. Distinct edge-ballot intersections contain at most one candidate, so higher ell≥2 cohesive groups cannot exist and JR=PJR=EJR. Four-state transfer forbids 00→00 exactly in active range, counts every PO valid word; Poisson factorial moments for zeros triple count yield mean t³/m² and limit e^(−λ³) when t/m^(2/3)→λ, while negative association for disjoint hypergeometric triples and overlap variance give high-deficit zero probability. Independently brute-enumerated 491 profiles with m=4..8 including all alternative k-committees to confirm PO and JR, and inspected verifier source. Infinite Poisson law rests on analytic moment bounds, not finite enumerations.
